question: What public callback metadata contract should generic Telegram agent turns receive for inline-button clicks?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the durable fix crosses Telegram callback identity, generic agent-visible metadata, current-message tool context, and dedupe semantics, so automation should not pick the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Expose separate source-message metadata
options.body: Preserve callback query id for event identity while adding source chat/message ids to agent metadata and current-message tool context.

options.title: Keep generic callbacks text-only
options.body: Document that editing the originating message is supported through registered plugin interactive handlers, not generic callback fallback turns.

options.title: Adopt and harden the open PR shape
options.body: Use the existing fork PR only as a starting point after adding the missing current-message wiring, tests, merge cleanup, and real Telegram proof.

recommendation.title: Expose separate source-message metadata
recommendation.body: Preserve callback query id for event identity while adding source chat/message ids to agent metadata and current-message tool context.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing owner from the shared channel/plugin runtime history and the decision spans Telegram plus core agent metadata contracts.
